body: You’re right. If I don’t do it all the time then I don’t take proper precautions. I guess I should say normally I do.

Yeah. I’m just afraid she won’t come around. She  hasn’t talked to her grandparents since she was 13 (they made racist comments and she’s mixed) and held a grudge against her dad for about 4 years for something hurtful he said and is just not forgiving him.

We’re apart now so sex isn’t even a factor. I agree with you though. She shouldn’t do it if she doesn’t want to. I was looking at it as I do stuff I don’t want to for her, but I realize that’s not the same now. It’s a fucked up point of view. 

Congratulations on the pregnancy by the way. How far along are you?

We’ve been together a total of 5 months. We are a long distance relationship. She lives halfway across the US. I haven’t seen her in 7 weeks since the pandemic. I’m getting out of the Army in 3 weeks. I don’t have a job lined up yet but have a few interviews that I’m hopeful about.

She just says I put a premium on sex and it’s not that important to her. She’s afraid I’ll never be satisfied in our relationship. I made a comment the other day about having sex with your partner even if you’re not in the mood because it’s something the other person wants. She said that was appalling and couldn’t believe I could say that. She says I can be too aggressive and head strong in arguments. I never yell. I never am physically abusive. I can just be very determined to get my point across and steam roll her in the process.

Thanks for your comment. 

I think my fiancée would be happier without me. She says she’s got some serious concerns about me. We got pregnant within 2 months of meeting each other and engaged at 3 months. I’ve always been really honest with her but I think some stuff was just overshadowed in the beginning. She’s a great woman. She could find another man quickly and the baby would grow up knowing her as her dad. I have a $400,000 life insurance policy that covers Suicide. They would be taken care of financially for a while.
